newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan electricity firms' profits fall in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Japan electricity firms' profits fall in 1996/97.

text.p: Japan's nine leading electric power utilities reported current profits of a combined 585.9 billion yen in the last business year, down 17.6 percent from a year earlier, an industry body said on Monday.
All nine firms reported that sales and profits fell in fiscal 1996/97 which ended March 31, the Federation of Electric Power Companies said.
It was the first time in nine years for the nine utilities to suffer declines in both sales and profits.
Current profit is pre-tax and includes gains and losses from investments.

Sales of electricity rose in volume by 2.3 percent in 1996/97 from a year earlier, however revenue fell by 0.1 percent to about 15.2 trillion yen because of the cut in electricity rates in January 1996, the federation said.

Although the nine utilities spent 7.4 percent less last year in maintenance costs, they were forced to spend more to procure energy resources because of higher crude oil prices and the weaker yen against the dollar.
The industry's nuclear power facility operating rate last year averaged 80.8 percent, little changed from 80.2 percent a year earlier.
